title: Prospective observational study on the benefits of pre-hospital Medical Intervention Units in Hesse
summary:
Over recent years, a steady increase in emergency physician deployments has been observed, particularly with an increasing proportion of non-critically injured and ill patients. In response to this, nationwide expansion of emergency physician-staffed rescue units has been implemented, although this has not yet been necessary in the district of Gießen. As a result, the experience of individual emergency physicians in treating critical patient groups is reduced. At the same time, there is an expectation of mastering advanced emergency medical techniques in pre-hospital emergency care. Such advanced emergency procedures (e.g., the placement of a thoracic drain for tension pneumothorax) are especially necessary for critically ill and severely injured patients, which may also be required in rare cases in pediatric emergency medicine. In both areas, it is not possible to acquire sufficient expertise in emergency medical services due to the low number of cases. This was demonstrated in studies on the reality of emergency physician operations in ground-based emergency medical services, where, for example, the probability of placing a thoracic drain was found to be over 6 years — expertise cannot be assumed in this area.

Such competencies can only be acquired through regular in-hospital care at specialized centers (e.g., at maximum care hospitals, university hospitals). For instance, at the University Hospital Gießen and Marburg GmbH, Gießen location, 3,575 children under 16 years of age received anesthesiological care in 2023, of whom 1,367 were intubated, and 1,085 were treated with a laryngeal mask. During the same period, 42 thoracic drain placements were performed in children. This issue was addressed in the ninth statement and recommendation of the Government Commission on the “Reform of Emergency and Acute Care: Emergency Services and Financing,” published in September 2023. Under Chapter II, "Initial Situation and Problems," it is noted that there is no uniform definition of what is considered a specialist standard in emergency services, which makes a uniform quality and qualification standard difficult to achieve.

The reform proposals suggest expanding the competencies of non-physician personnel (including curative measures) so that the resource of "emergency physician" is available for complex cases: "Accordingly, in the future, specially qualified emergency physicians should only be used pre-hospitally in particularly complex cases and mostly via rescue (transport) helicopters/air rescue or with telemedical support." Additionally, the establishment of "specialized rescue units" is explicitly recommended. In this context, Medical Intervention Units (MIU) could be a suitable means for treating patients who require complex interventions.

MIUs consist of expert teams with sufficient expertise and regular practice in treating complex disease or injury patterns. They reach the scene either by ground or air. In the case of ground-based rescue, they are defined as a "Medical Intervention Car" (MIC). Potential patient cohorts that, according to current scientific understanding, would benefit from specialized teams include those requiring resuscitation, those needing special invasive emergency techniques, severely injured patients, or critically ill children.

Current Situation for the Gießen Location 
On November 14, 2023, the "Gießen Medical Intervention Car (GiMIC)" project was presented in the working group "Structural Issues in Emergency Services" and approved on November 28, 2023, by the State Advisory Board for Emergency Services of the Hessian Ministry for Family, Seniors, Sports, Health, and Care for a 24-month trial period under the experimental clause of the Hessian Emergency Services Plan (see appendix). An extension of the project duration is possible. The primary goal of the project is to assess the benefit of MIUs and to identify factors relevant to the transferability of the concept to other locations in Hesse (e.g., MIU equipment). To date, the Gießen MIC is the only MIC approved by the Hessian Ministry for Family, Seniors, Sports, Health, and Care as an exception.

Note: 
The Hessian Ministry for Family, Seniors, Sports, Health, and Care (contact: Dr. Henrik Vollbracht) has indicated that any additional MIU locations should also be scientifically monitored. The following primary application is being submitted only for the Gießen district, as it will be the first MIU in Hesse. However, it is possible that further locations will be established within the next two years. Since a study database would already exist in Gießen, the Hessian Ministry for Family, Seniors, Sports, Health, and Care would refer to our clinic, so additional study centers could be included in the study. In such cases, the ethics committee would of course be informed separately, and an amendment would be requested. The goal is to generate the largest possible data base, as only a small number of cases per center is expected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients, regardless of age, who receive advanced emergency medical measures from GiMIC or other emergency services in the Gießen district during the study period will be included. Furthermore, incidents will be recorded in which GiMIC was alerted but no treatment was performed (e.g., due to the premature death of the patient or cancellation by other emergency services). Advanced emergency medical measures are defined as follows:

- Placement of thoracic drains
- Resuscitative thoracotomy
- Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA)
- Extracorporeal Cardiac Life Support (ECLS)
- Use of hemostatic agents
- Use of transfusions
- Use of tourniquets
- Treatment of critically ill or injured children under the age of 16, including the implementation of invasive and non-invasive ventilation, the establishment of intraosseous or intravenous access, or the use of the aforementioned measures.
Exclusion criteria:
Deployments without alerting GiMIC
